lesson.menu_title: Owning the Numbers -- Presenting Quarterly Results with Precision
lesson.menu_desc: Variance, the passive voice, and reporting a bad number without a defendant -- 37 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Owning the Numbers
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 4 -- Owning the Numbers
lesson.grammar_point: advanced passive voice for impersonal reporting

listenings.text: After twenty years of sitting on the other side of the table, I can tell you that a board asks the same three questions about any number, in the same order. The first is: is this comparable? Like for like, with the one-offs stripped out, is this the same thing we looked at last quarter? If you have not answered that before you are asked, the rest of your slide does not get heard. The second question is: is it going to happen again? People forgive a one-off. What they do not forgive is a one-off that turns up three quarters in a row wearing a different name. And the third question is the dangerous one, because everybody prepares the first two and forgets this one. What are you doing about it? And please, do not tell me you are monitoring it. Monitoring is not a fix. When a board hears we are monitoring the situation, what it hears is: no answer yet.

I use the passive voice all day long and I am not embarrassed about it. When the pipeline was not updated, the person who did not update it is not the information. Naming them in a board meeting moves everybody's attention to a person instead of a problem, and the problem is what we are there to solve. But there is a line, and the line is this. When the agent is you, say so. If it was my decision, I say I decided. The moment I say it was decided, everyone in that room starts hunting for the author, and they find me anyway, only now it looks like I tried to hide. The other half of the rule matters just as much. Good news always takes the active voice. Somebody built that result, and if I say the result was achieved, I have quietly stolen it from them. So: the passive for the problem, my own name for my own decisions, and their names for anything that went right. What a board is really testing is not the number. It is whether you know which parts of it are yours.

extra_audio.text: The forecast was missed by nine percent in Argentina. The pipeline had not been updated since May, and two renewals were counted twice. The reconciliation is being rebuilt this quarter. It is expected that the run rate will be recovered by December.

paras: Growth of eleven percent year on year was recorded across the region. Like for like, with the Colombian acquisition stripped out, the figure is six percent, against a market benchmark of four. The margin was held, and the claims experience in the south was offset by corporate renewals, which were driven by the commercial team in Brazil.

One variance requires explanation. In Argentina the forecast was missed by nine percent. The pipeline had not been updated since May, and two renewals were counted twice at the point of consolidation. Neither issue is expected to repeat: the reconciliation is being rebuilt this quarter and a second review point has been added before consolidation.
It is expected that the Argentine run rate will be recovered by December. The currency moved during the period, but not materially, and it does not account for the variance.

Two items are flagged for the board. Climate exposure in the south has grown with the portfolio and the limits have not been revised since February. A decision on those limits is requested this quarter.
reading.source: Internal note -- Commercial Directorate, Latin America

gist.prompt: What is this note mainly doing?
choices: Explaining one bad market and asking the board to replace the local team
Reporting a good quarter, explaining the one variance in it, and asking for a decision
Announcing a change in how the region will be measured next year

items: Like for like, growth was higher than the market benchmark.
the figure is six percent, against a market benchmark of four.

The pipeline had not been updated since May -- no person is named anywhere in the note.
The currency movement explains the Argentine variance.
The currency moved during the period, but not materially, and it does not account for the variance.
